business_scope.primary_industry_name: Polyresin Vacuum Casting and Hand-Painted Limited Edition Statues

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Hong Kong SAR applies the Common Law under the Basic Law, while the mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) formation component applies PRC Civil Law, Partnership Enterprise Law and Foreign Investment Law.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) Investment Agreement
Agreement Between the Mainland and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income
Mainland and Hong Kong CEPA Agreement on Trade in Services
China-Singapore Bilateral Investment Treaty for conduit investment routed through Singapore

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (as amended), PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019), the Administration Measures for Beneficial Owner Information jointly issued by PBOC and SAMR as Order No. 3 (2024), effective November 1, 2024, and the Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) together with Part 11A of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) for the Significant Controllers Register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Certificate of Registration for the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation for the PRC FIP; Hong Kong Companies Registry if the Hong Kong SAR entity is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If originating in a Hague Apostille state (including Hong Kong SAR): notarize with a local notary, then obtain an Apostille from the Hong Kong High Court or PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular legalization is required. If originating in a non-Apostille state: notarize locally, then authenticate through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then obtain consular legalization from the PRC consulate or embassy; the two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Current Status and Business Registration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry; in China, the SAMR-registered entity credit record issued through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same mutually exclusive rule: Hague Apostille route for Contracting Parties (Hong Kong High Court Apostille) or consular legalization route for non-Contracting Parties; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Written Consent of Partners and Power of Attorney appointing the local filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The Hong Kong investor company or the PRC FIP partners through a notarized corporate minute
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in China: notarize in Hong Kong and obtain an Apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong SAR; for use in a non-Apostille jurisdiction: notarize and obtain consular legalization from the destination embassy or consulate. Apostille and legalization are alternative routes, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Limited Partnership Agreement including the FIP Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partners and law firm under PRC Partnership Enterprise Law or Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance; certified by competent authority or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the jurisdiction of issuance if that state is an Apostille member; otherwise consular legalization through the destination state consulate; never chain apostille and legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Institutional KYC Package
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing relationship bank of the investor or proposed local bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The original bank letter must be notarized if required and then apostilled if the issuer is in an Apostille member state, or legalized by the destination consulate if the issuer is in a non-member state; the letter remains valid for 90 days from issue.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Filing and AML/CFT Compliance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance counsel or the designated SAMR/PBOC data filing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Government filing is direct; certified copies for cross-border use are notarized and then either apostilled or consular-legalized depending on destination state; never chain both methods.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all natural-person beneficial owners, general partners, limited partners above 25%, directors, authorized signatories and ultimate controlling parties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK sanctions lists, the PRC terrorist organization list, Hong Kong sanctions lists and a minimum of 150 PEP watchlist sources. Screening must occur at onboarding, on any ownership or signatory change, and continuously using a commercially reasonable automation tool. OFAC 50 percent rule and UK/HK ownership-based sanctions aggregation must be applied. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence and filing of a suspicious transaction report to the FIU where required. Names must be screened in Chinese, English, and romanized forms with fuzzy matching at a minimum threshold of 85 percent, with false-positive analysis documented and retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: PRC SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform (name pre-approval and reservation module) and Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) Cyber Search Centre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For the PRC FIP, the statutory name must be in Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier naming format: administrative division plus distinctive name plus industry or operating characteristics plus organizational form such as Foreign-Invested Partnership. A Hong Kong investor may include a phonetic transliteration of its English name, but the registered Chinese name is controlling. For the Hong Kong SAR entity, English and Chinese names are

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 1997, amended 2006), Articles 8, 9, 10, 12, 14 and 34; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 12 and 31; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships (State Council Decree No. 567, effective 1 March 2010); Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Registration; for the Hong Kong SAR investor, Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) govern corporate capacity and continuing registration evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation of the registered office within Mainland China; the Hong Kong SAR Companies Registry is the issuing authority for the Hong Kong investor's corporate capacity and good standing certificates, not for the PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Partnership (SAMR unified registration form) together with the statutory Partnership Agreement and a legalized identification set for all foreign partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Foreign-Invested Partnership and no blocked escrow account rule under PRC law. Partners may agree on a contribution schedule in the Partnership Agreement. However, any inbound foreign investment must be settled through a duly opened domestic capital contribution account under SAFE rules, and capital contributions must be genuinely paid and booked before any distribution to partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (FORMED UNDER THE PARTNERSHIP LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA AND THE REGULATIONS ON REGISTRATION ADMINISTRATION OF FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIPS). WHEREAS the Partnership is proposed to be formed as a Foreign-Invested Partnership and the Partnership Agreement together with the Capital Contribution Schedule and all formation documents have been examined by the undersigned general partners; and WHEREAS the partners desire to approve the initial capital subscription, adopt the registered office, authorize the opening of banking accounts, and appoint the statutory officers for the purpose of completing registration, licensing, and commercial operations. NOW, THEREFORE, the general partners and management committee adopt the following resolutions: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION. The initial capital contribution of the Partnership in the amount stated in the Capital Contribution Schedule is hereby approved and ratified. Each partner is directed and authorized to contribute its subscribed amount to the Partnership's designated capital contribution account on or before the agreed payment date, and the managing general partner is directed to issue contribution receipts, maintain a capital register, and record non-cash contributions only after an independent appraisal obtained in accordance with PRC valuation rules. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office address of the Partnership, as set forth in the Partnership Registration Application and the supporting domicile proof, is hereby adopted. The managing general partner is authorized to execute and record the lease, utility contracts, and online address filings and to maintain the Partnership's statutory books and seal at that office. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The commercial bank designated in the application is approved as the Partnership's principal settlement bank. The managing general partner, the finance officer, and such other authorized signatories as the managing partner may name are jointly and severally authorized to open basic deposit, general settlement, foreign exchange, and capital contribution accounts, and to execute all account mandates, wire instructions, foreign exchange filings, and deposit agreements. The bank is expressly authorized to receive preorder deposits, refunds, and settlement proceeds from Stripe and PayPal in the Partnership's legal name. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following officers are appointed: managing general partner and chief executive; compliance and anti-money-laundering officer; finance officer; and partnership secretary. The officers are authorized to sign and file applications with SAMR, the tax authority, the foreign exchange authority, the ecological and environmental authority, the fire rescue authority, and the industrial product licensing authority; to engage a company secretary and legal counsel; and to execute all ancillary documents, declarations, and undertakings necessary to effectuate the formation, licensing, and lawful operation of the Partnership. 5. EFFECTIVENESS AND COUNTERPARTS. These resolutions are effective immediately and continue in force until revoked by a written instrument executed by all general partners. They may be executed in counterparts, in electronic or physical form, and each counterpart shall be deemed an original.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign-Investor Capacity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Name Registration System and the online one-stop business registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name pre-approval application using the SAMR unified registration platform. The proposed name must include the organizational form Foreign-Invested Partnership or FIP where required, must not conflict with a registered trademark or existing enterprise name, and must accurately reflect the business scope of manufacturing resin statues and collectible garage kits. Foreign partners must provide legalized certificates of incorporation or passports, apostille or consular legalization, certified Chinese translations, and a resolution authorizing the establishment of the PRC partnership. The authority will verify the foreign investor's capacity and issue a name approval notice valid for six months. No business activities may commence before name approval is granted.
required_dossiers: Proposed name application and explanation of meaning
Foreign investor's certificate of incorporation or passport
Certificate of good standing from the Hong Kong SAR Companies Registry
Apostilled or consular-legalized identity documents and certified Chinese translation
Partnership Agreement draft
Power of attorney and identity of the local formation agent
Commitment letter confirming lawful use of the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or foreign-investor qualification is queried, submit a written explanation and amended name within 10 business days. If the suspension is caused by missing legalization or translation, cure by obtaining a corrected apostille, consular certification, and certified translation. A final refusal may be appealed by administrative reconsideration before SAMR or by an administrative lawsuit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office at the proposed registered office in Mainland China, with legal counsel for the partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene all general and limited partners to execute the bilingual Partnership Agreement. The Agreement must specify the partnership name, registered address, business scope, capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management and voting rights, withdrawal and admission of partners, dispute resolution, and the liability of general and limited partners. Foreign partner signatures on corporate resolutions and powers of attorney must be notarized in the home jurisdiction, authenticated by apostille or consular legalization, and translated into Chinese by an authorized translation service. If a partner contributes machinery, intellectual property, premises, or other non-cash assets, an independent appraisal report must be obtained under PRC appraisal standards and attached to the notarial record. The notarized Partnership Agreement becomes the governing constitutional document for the FIP.
required_dossiers: Bilingual or Chinese Partnership Agreement
Original and counterpart execution pages
Foreign partner's notarized board or owner resolution
Power of attorney for the PRC formation representative
Capital contribution subscription and payment schedule
Notarized certificates of foreign partner signatures
Non-cash contribution valuation and transfer undertakings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary office rejects the document, obtain a conformed cross-check of foreign signatures and a notarized certificate of good standing from the Hong Kong Companies Registry. A supplemental execution page may be signed by all partners, and a new notarial certificate must be issued before filing. If valuation of non-cash assets is disputed, appoint an independent PRC-qualified appraiser.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Foreign-Invested Partnership Registration Application with SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or the equivalent free-trade-zone registration authority where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Partnership through the SAMR online one-stop portal or the physical registration hall. Attach the executed and notarized Partnership Agreement, foreign partners' legalized identification certificates, domicile proof, capital contribution subscription list, authorization forms, and the managing partner's passport or resident identity document. The SAMR officer will examine the name, business scope, registered address, capital contribution schedule, partner liability structure, and legality of the business purpose. Upon acceptance, sign the electronic application and proceed with the issuance of the Partnership Business License and Unified Social Credit Code. The partnership must not begin manufacturing, open a settlement bank account, or receive preorders before the business license is issued.
required_dossiers: Signed SAMR Foreign-Invested Partnership registration application
Notarized Partnership Agreement
Foreign investor identity or registration documents
Apostilled or legalized certificates and certified translations
Proof of registered office address or lease certificate
Capital contribution subscription deed
General or managing partner identification documents
Power of attorney and agent identification
Legal business commitment letter describing ISIC 3240 operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR suspends or returns the application, correct the identified defects and resubmit within 15 business days. If foreign qualification documents are defective, provide newly notarized and apostilled certificates. If the application is rejected on substantive grounds, file an administrative reconsideration with the next-level SAMR or bring an administrative lawsuit within the statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Engraving, Public Security Filing, and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB)-licensed seal engraving enterprise; Municipal Tax Service under the State Taxation Administration; SAMR post-registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Partnership Business License, procure the partnership seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and the managing partner's personal seal from a PSB-licensed engraver. File the seal impressions with the Public Security Bureau and SAMR and obtain the seal filing certificate. Then complete tax registration electronically using the Unified Social Credit Code, activate value-added tax invoice issuance, and determine whether the partnership should be registered as a general VAT taxpayer. The tax registration must include stamp duty, corporate income tax, and payroll-related registration. Maintain authenticated copies of tax certificates and seal records in the statutory corporate governance register.
required_dossiers: Partnership Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
FIP registration notification
Managing partner identification and legalized passport copy
PSB seal filing form and seal specimen card
Power of attorney for seal engraving
Tax registration information form and responsible persons list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal filing is rejected, resubmit a corrected PSB application with identity proof and a notarized power of attorney. If tax registration is delayed, activate the e-tax identity through the SAMR application and bind the tax responsible person within three working days. Any tax registration discrepancy should be cured by filing a written rectification with the Municipal Tax Service before invoices are issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, SAFE Foreign-Exchange Registration, and Merchant Settlement Configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the PRC designated by the partnership, with State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) reporting through the bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the basic deposit account, general settlement account, and, if required, a foreign currency capital account to receive the Hong Kong investor's inbound contribution and operating receipts. Complete the bank's customer due diligence and beneficial ownership questionnaire for all partners, including corporate certificates and personal identification. Register the Foreign-Invested Partnership with SAFE through the bank's FDI and foreign exchange information system so that future capital contributions, profit distributions, and foreign remittances are lawful. After the settlement account is active, configure the Stripe and PayPal merchant accounts in the Partnership's legal name, using the bank as the payout institution. Keep AML classification at the standard risk tier and document the source of funds for all preorder deposits received before product shipment.
required_dossiers: Partnership Business License and FIP registration certificate
Seal filing certificate and specimen card
Notarized Partnership Agreement
Beneficial ownership and AML/KYC declarations
Hong Kong investor's certificate of good standing and directors' register
Managing partner and authorized signatory identification
Registered office lease and utility proof
Bank account opening application and specimen form
Expected transaction volume and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence due to the Hong Kong SAR investor, supply updated certificates of good standing, a consolidated UBO chart, and pro-forma financial statements. If the bank still refuses, apply to another commercial bank and, if necessary, file a written complaint with the People's Bank of China or the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Industrial, Fire, and Occupational Licensing Pre-Operation Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Ecology and Environment Bureau under the Ministry of Ecology and Environment; SAMR Industrial Product Production License Office; Fire and Rescue division of the Ministry of Emergency Management; local Work Safety and Occupational Health authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before starting physical production, submit the EIA classification form or full EIA report to the local Ecology and Environment Bureau and obtain the corresponding acceptance or registration certificate. For resin casting and hand painting, prepare a pollution prevention plan covering volatile organic compound controls, hazardous waste storage, and wastewater pretreatment. Concurrently apply for fire protection design review and fire safety acceptance certificate from the Fire and Rescue authority, and arrange structural load inspection for casting benches and paint booths. If the resin statues fall within the toy product catalogue, apply for the industrial product production license or CCC-type certification as applicable. Register the workplace occupational hazard evaluation and initiate annual monitoring for styrene, dust, and noise. Physical production may begin only after the EIA, fire, industrial safety, and occupational health clearances are obtained.
required_dossiers: EIA registration form or full EIA report
Production process description for ISIC 3240 resin casting
Raw material resin MSDS and VOC content data
Wastewater pretreatment design and discharge agreement
Hazardous waste storage plan and disposal contract
Fire safety design drawings and fire load calculation
Structural load certificate for casting and paint booth areas
Application for fire safety acceptance certificate
Occupational hazard evaluation and workplace monitoring plan
Toy product industrial production license or CCC application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EIA or fire application is rejected, remediate by installing VOC abatement equipment, revising the emergency response plan, and resubmitting monitoring data. If a certificate is suspended, operations must cease pending field verification and reissue. Any final denial may be appealed through administrative reconsideration or litigation within statutory time limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Industrial Product Production License Office; local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation; Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) local Bureau; Fire and Rescue department of the Ministry of Emergency Management.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Toy Product Industrial Production License and/or China Compulsory Product Certification where the resin statue falls within the toy product catalogue; Environmental Impact Assessment Approval or Registration; Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate; and Occupational Hazard Evaluation and Work-Safety Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China, delegated to the provincial or municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Full EIA Report Form for resin casting and spray hand-painting lines with VOC emission controls; Category III - EIA Registration Form may apply only to low-output hand-painting and assembly without resin casting, provided annual VOC solvent consumption is below 10 tonnes and no hazardous waste treatment is performed. A full EIA Report is mandatory where the operation involves chemical treatment or storage of hazardous waste.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), online through the National Unified Electronic Tax Service Platform at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn; administrative supervision is also exercised through the provincial and municipal local tax bureaus where the Foreign-Invested Partnership is domiciled.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Foreign non-resident partners execute a partnership agreement and register the Foreign-Invested Partnership with the local office of the State Administration for Market Regulation, obtaining a Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code. Step 2: Through the multi-license integration one-stop reform, tax registration is completed simultaneously with commercial registration; within 30 days after license issuance or commencement of operations, the FIP must complete supplementary tax registration on the Electronic Tax Service Platform, file its financial accounting system record, report its bank deposit accounts, and complete real-name authentication for the legal representative, financial officer, and authorized tax agents. Step 3: The Unified Social Credit Code is used as the definitive Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN); the competent tax authority determines the VAT taxpayer identity (general VAT taxpayer if annual assessable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, otherwise small-scale taxpayer) and sets the filing cadence (monthly or quarterly). Step 4: The entity must apply for invoice allotment and type authorization on the fully digitalized electronic invoice service platform, thereby opening its Digital Tax Account; no separate VAT registration certificate is issued. Step 5: When making China-source payments to non-resident partners, the FIP must register as a withholding agent and obtain the statutory non-resident withholding tax registration reference for remittances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (the PRC has no check-the-box entity classification regime; pass-through treatment of the partnership is mandatory, with the FIP outside the scope of Corporate Income Tax and each partner taxed on its distributive share under Cai Shui [2008] No. 159). Elective instruments available are restricted to: the choice between small-scale and general VAT taxpayer status when below the mandatory threshold, simplified VAT assessment for certain prescribed supplies, and the contractual allocation of partnership profits among resident and non-resident partners, all subject to transfer pricing and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual assessable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 under the STA Order No. 43 General VAT Taxpayer Registration Measures; below that threshold, the entity remains a small-scale taxpayer eligible for the statutory VAT exemption of monthly sales up to RMB 100,000 or quarterly sales up to RMB 300,000, extended by Ministry of Finance / STA Public Notice No. 19 of 2023 through 31 December 2027.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The FIP must issue fully digitalized electronic invoices through the State Taxation Administration's Electronic Invoice Service Platform and its Digital Tax Account; every invoice is transmitted to the tax authority in real time at issuance as structured XML/JSON data bearing a mandatory anti-fraud digital stamp and QR code, without reliance on legacy tax-control disks; high-volume exporters may integrate via the STA enterprise digital API (Le Qi platform) for automated invoice clearance, export confirmation, and reconciliations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Polyresin statue goods qualify for the 0% VAT export rate when physically exported from the Chinese customs territory, provided: (i) the FIP holds general VAT taxpayer status and files the export refund/exemption mechanism applicable to manufacturing exporters (exemption, credit, and refund method under Cai Shui [2012] No. 39 and the Interim VAT Regulations); (ii) the goods are declared to and cleared by customs, with electronic clearance data successfully matched by the STA; (iii) the sale is made to an overseas customer with consideration payable in foreign currency; (iv) the goods carry lawful input VAT credits evidenced by compliant purchase invoices; and (v) export proceeds are repatriated through bank channels within the statutory 180-day window and the export revenue is declared in the VAT period, with the refund application submitted no later than 30 April of the following year. Cross-border digital supplies and offshore-related services are eligible for zero rating only under the criteria of Cai Shui [2016] No. 36, namely consumption entirely outside China and settlement in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration Form) showing electronic clearance and release status
Full-set original Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal/air waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from China
Export commercial invoice and packing list consistent with the declared customs value

Bank foreign-currency collection receipt (export proceeds transaction slip) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange trade-monitoring verification record confirming inward remittance of the export proceeds
Input VAT special invoices or fully digitalized e-invoices for the exported goods, together with the export-typed digital ordinary invoice issued for the overseas sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is continuously monitored through three-way electronic cross-validation among tax, customs, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange trade-forex data. The STA may defer, suspend, or verify export refunds through correspondence investigations, on-site tax audits, or asset inspections. Where zero-rating is unsubstantiated, or where export proceeds are not collected within 180 days of customs clearance without an approved statutory exception, the transaction is reclassified as an inland taxable sale: the VAT shortfall is clawed back, a late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% per day of the overdue tax, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax is imposed under Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law. Fabricated documentation or collusion to claim fraudulent refunds constitutes the criminal offense of fraudulent export tax refund under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, punishable by fines and imprisonment escalating to life, together with disqualification from the export refund regime and public listing on the tax dishonesty blacklist.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The operative central bank authority is the People's Bank of China (PBOC) acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership, with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervising the linked Hong Kong SAR treasury and clearing node.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The entity is a PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership, so the convertibility regime is that of the People's Republic of China. RMB is fully convertible for current account trade items, but capital account movements remain strictly regulated. Foreign partner capital contributions require FDI registration at SAFE, a dedicated foreign-exchange capital account with a PRC bank, and the funds must be used in accordance with the filed partnership business scope. Profit distributions from accumulated partnership earnings are treated as current account transactions for remittance purposes after tax compliance, but the remitting bank must be provided with audited financial statements, a partner distribution resolution, tax clearance, and the appropriate SAFE payment and filing code. A significant profit remittance hurdle is that distributions to overseas partners require the bank to verify that the partnership has no pending Chinese tax liabilities, and the non-resident partner must provide withholding tax certificates proving that the relevant corporate or individual income tax has been paid or exempted. Surplus capital or capital reductions, by contrast, are capital account items and cannot be freely remitted without SAFE approval. There is no legal parity for automatic outbound conversion of not-yet-earned capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For physical export sales from the PRC FIP, the statutory rule is mandatory repatriation rather than mandatory surrender: all export foreign-exchange receipts must be brought back to a domestic SAFE-designated foreign exchange settlement account no later than the contracted trade payment date or, in the normal goods-trade monitoring cycle, within 90 days after export customs clearance if no different commercial term is declared. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the FIP may retain 100% of the proceeds in foreign currency or sell any amount to an eligible bank at market rate. The receipts must be electronically matched with the customs declaration numbers under the SAFE Goods-Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System; non-repatriation, fake declarations, or excessive retention overseas trigger removal from the enterprise trusted list and escalation to physical-inspection status.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability and, for the PRC FIP, legally prohibited as a primary treasury account provider. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Airwallex and similar entities do not hold a PBOC/CBIRC commercial banking license in mainland China and therefore cannot open a basic RMB deposit account, receive SAFE-registered FDI capital injections, or remit profits through the SAFE current-account framework. An HK-authorised money service operator could serve an HK corporate treasury node for offshore collections and disbursements, but it cannot replace the onshore Tier-1 bank, and any offshore EMI settlement into China must ultimately be repatriated through a licensed bank under SAFE trade-monitoring rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory. The PRC FIP must present its executive partner or a formally appointed PRC legal representative and authorized signatory with a valid national ID and the entity seal at the bank branch for the basic deposit account interview; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for this mandatory face-to-face identity verification. A non-resident HK general partner can evidence its authority through apostilled or consularized notarized board resolutions and a notarized partnership agreement, but the designated PRC manager must still appear in person and sign the account opening documents under dual-control KYC procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented cross-border e-commerce collections through Stripe and PayPal are unreconciled to shipping declarations, creating a trade-flow mismatch under SAFE goods-trade monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Month-by-month gateway settlement reports, order-level transaction data, customer and refund records, warehouse dispatch logs, bill-of-lading or airway-bill copies, customs export declaration numbers, and a bank-facing trade-flow reconciliation ledger mapping each aggregated settlement to the underlying pre-order and shipment event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A HK-registered general partner with indirect offshore ownership creates a beneficial-ownership confidence gap for the PRC bank compliance committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete ownership chain from the FIP to every HK and offshore intermediary and to the ultimate natural persons, supported by the partnership agreement, registered partner register, HK Business Registration certificate, incorporation certificates, director registers, Hong Kong Significant Controllers Register extract, tax residence certificates, certified passports, apostille or consular legalization, and PRC translation of all non-English documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large pre-order deposit inflows arriving before physical shipment resemble transaction layering or unperformed trade activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product launch and pre-order commercial terms, third-party e-commerce marketplace contracts, refund and chargeback logs, production capacity evidence, ERP order books, historical dispatch data, and a written liquidity projection showing expected deposit peaks and the timing between collection, production and shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring outbound payments to overseas IP licensors and suppliers present a goods-versus-services or royalty misclassification and potential profit-stripping risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed license, distribution and raw-material supply agreements, IP registration certificates, applicable withholding tax remittance certificates or tax exemption forms, SAFE current-account payment and purpose codes, customs and invoice evidence for physical goods imports, and an allocation or transfer-pricing memorandum demonstrating commercial reasonableness.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign partner contribution funds must move via SWIFT MT103 from the HK remitter to the FIP's dedicated SAFE-registered FDI foreign-exchange capital account at a PRC Tier-1 bank. The remittance must carry a clear purpose description such as Foreign investment contribution to Foreign-Invested Partnership, and the receiving bank must report the inward transaction using the SAFE international receipts and payments transaction coding for direct-investment capital injection. After credit, the FIP should instruct the bank to convert to RMB and transfer to the basic operational account only after submitting the capital utilisation declaration. For capital verification, the FIP engages a PRC certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report; the bank's inward credit slip, SAFE foreign exchange registration form, and fund usage vouchers are the supporting dossiers. The FIP must not allow Stripe or PayPal treasury flows to be used as nominal FDI contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and trade settlements should be executed using SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic transfers for invoice-based goods and services, commercial letters of credit via SWIFT MT700 or MT707 for large purchase orders, and documentary collections on DP or DA terms for lower-risk repeat shipments. Each outward payment must be backed by the underlying purchase or sales contract, invoice, packing list, transport documents and customs declarations where applicable, and must be declared with the correct SAFE trade payment purpose code. For domestic suppliers and raw materials inside mainland China, the FIP should use the domestic CNY clearing rails, specifically the China National Advanced Payment System large-value real-time gross settlement rail, rather than converting foreign currency unnecessarily. For funds from Stripe and PayPal pre-order settlements received offshore, the offshore treasury account should aggregate and repatriate through MT103 to the FIP's onshore bank account with the platform payout reconciliation attached so that each aggregated receipt can be traced to identifiable customers and order events.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based RMB against foreign-exchange forward contracts with a PRC Tier-1 bank, limited to the amount and tenor of a documented trade or partnership capital exposure.

Foreign-exchange swaps combining a spot transaction and a forward transaction to manage short-term liquidity between the RMB operational account and the foreign-currency capital or settlement account.

Cross-currency swaps, including fixed-for-floating structures in RMB and other currencies, only when matched to an existing debt, intra-group funding, or multi-year procurement commitment in the same currencies and residual maturity.

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed only by the HK parent company as an offshore hedge of expected economic exposure; the onshore PRC FIP itself is not permitted to use onshore NDFs.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at partnership entity level (Hong Kong FIP is fiscally transparent); partners are taxed on their allocated share at 16.5% for corporate partners and 15% for non-corporate partners, with two-tiered relief of 8.25% / 7.5% on the first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong imposes no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax, no VAT/GST and no sales tax. Profits sourced wholly outside Hong Kong are exempt under the territorial principle. Two-tiered profits tax applies; no bespoke exemption for resin statue e-commerce manufacturing.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no time limit); carry-back is not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return Form BIR52 (Sole Proprietorship / Partnership), filed through the IRD eTax electronic portal (www.etax.gov.hk) or in paper at the Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (year of assessment runs 1 April to 31 March; BIR52 is issued after the relevant accounting period).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due by the date specified on the issued tax return, normally within one month of the issue date; standard issues on 1 April are due by 2 May. Tax representatives can obtain extensions based on the accounting year-end (e.g. a 31 December year-end extended due date is usually 15 August of the assessment year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal and business names of all partners, Hong Kong business registration number, principal place of business, correspondence address and email.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-invested FIP, list each non-resident partner and appoint a Hong Kong tax representative; state the partner's country of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return; must match the partnership's financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident FIPs should use a period aligned with the controlling partner's audited accounts; gaps in the period must be separately reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box P1 / P2 - Gross Sales and Receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from sales of resin statues, preorder deposits, shipping charges and other receipts, net of returns and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all Stripe and PayPal receivables, including customer preorder deposits, and separately identify income sourced in Hong Kong vs. mainland China in an attached schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box P11 - Net Profit per Accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss after all deductible operating expenses, except partner drawings and personal expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For pass-through purposes, report the partnership's profit before partner profit-sharing allocations; interest paid to partners on capital is deductible only if genuine and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back schedule for depreciation, provisions, private expenses, fines, gifts over prescribed caps and expenditures lacking proper vouchers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must disallow home-office, travel and vehicle costs unless directly attributable to the resin statue business and supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional schedule substantiating any claim that profits arose wholly outside Hong Kong, e.g. sales concluded and delivered abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide e-commerce platform statements, courier logs, manufacturing contracts and negotiation records proving that no essential profit-generating activity took place in Hong Kong.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts: (i) fixed penalty up to HK$10,000; (ii) daily default surcharge of up to HK$300 per day while non-compliance continues; (iii) estimated assessments under IRO s. 82; (iv) late payment surcharges of 5% then 10%; and (v) if negligence or intent is established, up to three times the amount of tax undercharged.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose any withholding tax on dividends, profit distributions or partnership distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A partner seeking Mainland China - Hong Kong DTA relief must: (1) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate through IRD Form IR1313A; (2) provide a certificate of beneficial ownership; and (3) file the treaty claim with the Chinese tax authority in the annual enterprise income tax reconciliation / foreign tax credit return. Partnerships themselves are not entitled to treaty benefits; each partner must individually prove residence and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of intellectual property in Hong Kong are deemed assessable profits under IRO s.21A, taxed on a gross basis at 16.5% for corporate recipients / 15% for non-corporate recipients; treaty relief for Mainland China residents reduces the rate to 7%. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to any Hong Kong withholding tax unless the recipient carries on a Hong Kong business through a permanent establishment; under the DTA the source-side cap is 7%. No withholding applies to dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: HK$4,000,000 per controlled transaction category for property and services, HK$4,000,000 for financing transactions, and HK$2,000,000 for intangible-controlled transactions; Master File obligations arise for taxpayers with annual gross income exceeding HK$200,000,000 that also meet the controlled transaction threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing like the UAE or BVI, but the IRD applies strong economic-substance requirements through the territorial source doctrine, anti-avoidance rules (IRO ss. 61 and 61A), and DTA benefit limitation principles. A foreign-invested partnership that maintains no office, no staff, no board minutes and no risk-management functions in Hong Kong will fail an offshore profits claim and may be treated as a shell for treaty and AML purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Stripe and PayPal receivables from BIR52, diverting customer preorder deposits to personal bank accounts, or falsely labelling Hong Kong sales as offshore without any supporting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate penalty up to HK$10,000 plus three times the tax undercharged under IRO s.82A; 5%/10% late payment surcharges; criminal prosecution leading to a fine and imprisonment for up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are personally and severally liable for all assessed tax and penalties; where a corporate partner acts as general partner, its directors who consented or connived are personally liable; tax warrants may lead to asset seizure, garnishment, and court-ordered travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Hong Kong FIP as a letterbox that holds e-commerce payment flow only, while all purchasing, manufacturing, order-taking and management decisions occur in mainland China; claiming offshore profits and treaty benefits without demonstrable Hong Kong substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD will re-source 100% of the profit as Hong Kong-source taxable income; anti-avoidance provisions allow re-characterization of transactions, denial of treaty relief, and an additional GAAR penalty of up to 100% of the tax saved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The unlimited general partner is personally liable on any evasion found; directors of corporate general partners may be assessed jointly for unpaid tax; in flagrant cases, the court may issue a proprietary estoppel, freeze assets, and place the responsible individuals on a departure-prevention list.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / money laundering through payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the FIP's bank account to receive preorder deposits and immediately transferring funds to mainland personal accounts or cryptocurrency wallets; manufacturing fake purchase orders from shell suppliers to justify the layers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 455), conviction for dealing with tainted property carries a fine of up to HK$5,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 14 years, plus confiscation of the proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any partner or senior officer who knows or has reasonable grounds to believe the funds are proceeds of crime is equally liable; post-charge, defendants may be subject to travel bans, passport surrender, and asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a 30% gross-sales royalty to a mainland related party that has no active IP development; entering into undocumented intercompany finance or service arrangements; failing to prepare or retain Local File and Master File despite controlled transactions exceeding the HK$4,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length royalty (normally zero) under IRO s.50A; penalty for failure to keep records of up to HK$100,000; understatement negligence penalty up to three times the tax shortfall; full interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and any shadow director of a corporate partner can be held jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax; commercial bankruptcy proceedings may be commenced against them personally to enforce the debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit BIR52 for two consecutive years, ignoring IRD estimated assessments, dissolving the partnership without notifying IRD, or leaving Hong Kong before filing while continuing e-commerce sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD issues an estimated assessment using maximum presumable profits; fixed fine of HK$10,000 plus a daily penalty of HK$300; a 5% late-payment surcharge after six months and an additional 10% after one year; judgment can lead to repossession of stock and bank balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner remains personally liable even after dissolution; a tax debt certificate can be filed in court, allowing bailiffs to seize partnership and personal assets; persistent non-compliance may result in an arrest warrant and extradition proceedings if the partner flees the jurisdiction.
